tier_reason: Only first-party numbers exist (Dropbox 2016 post, seen via two independent search snippets because dropbox.tech fails DNS here) with C flags and CPU but no public benchmark code or Rust toolchain/flags; the independent reports (rust-brotli issue #76, android-doctor issue #74) give timings without full methodology. Every figure shows the Rust code slower than the C reference.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Not faster than C. Dropbox post (search snippets only): the safe Rust decompressor ran at 72% of the speed of the vanilla gcc-4.9 -O3 C decompressor on 4 MB blocks, 217 MB/s on an Intel Core i7-4790 @ 3.60GHz; turning off allocator zeroing raised it to 224 MB/s (+3.2%, derived from page data) and the unsafe feature (no bounds checks, no memory initialisation) to 249 MB/s, 82% of the C code. Author's 2017 Hacker News comment (snippet only): about 80-90% of the original's speed on average, with some files compressing faster in Rust than with the original codec. Independent: android-doctor issue #74 (2026-10-03) measured brotli crate 9.0 decode at 250 MB/s against 391 MB/s for the C reference (1.56x slower) on 10-core Apple Silicon, and 4.65 s against 2.28 s (2.04x) on firmware images. The book's 'over 10 percent after removing initialization and bounds checking' compares the port with its own earlier version, not with C.
corrections.caveats: Does not beat the baseline on any number found: every figure puts Rust at or below C. The 72% / 217 / 224 / 249 MB/s / 82% figures come from search-result snippets of the Dropbox post (2016, i7-4790, gcc-4.9 -O3 C baseline, 4 MB blocks); dropbox.tech could not be opened in this session (DNS failure), so they are snippet only, though two separate snippets agree. The post measured decompression, whose code lives in dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor (a dependency of this crate), not in this repo; no Rust compiler version or flags were given and no benchmark code is published. The Hacker News comment (news.ycombinator.com/item?id=14903412) is a 2017 self-report seen only as a snippet, with no per-file numbers, CPU or flags. The repo README makes no speed claim; the decompressor README lists the expected losses against C (extra hgroup indirection, bounds checks on every access, no aligned 64/128-bit loads from a byte slice). Independent reports show Rust slower than C: github.com/dropbox/rust-brotli/issues/76 (comment, 2023-05-13) reports decompressing a 50 GB texture tarball in 160 s against 90 s (the comment does not name which tool took which time, context implies Rust was slower; hardware, flags and quality not stated); github.com/Vaibhav91one/android-doctor/issues/74 measured brotli crate 9.0 decode at 250 MB/s against 391 MB/s for the C reference via Python brotli on a 10-core Apple Silicon release build (no flags or C version stated), and a later comment 4.65 s against 2.28 s (2.04x) on firmware images. A later Dropbox post (Broccoli, snippet only) mentions a decompression bug in rust-brotli-decompressor that Dropbox patched upstream. No public benchmark code with compiler, flags and CPU exists, so tier A and B do not apply. Flagged entry: notable and maintained (9.0.0 released 2026-09-02), but a safety-first port that is slower than C.

notes: Reject as not-faster on valid evidence (miniz precedent); under the keep-and-document rule the orchestrator may override to keep with the not-faster shortcoming, since the record itself is honest about it and the crate is notable (953 stars, widely used brotli crate). Metadata confirmed: BSD-3-Clause AND MIT (sidebar and Cargo.toml), 953 stars, last commit 2026-09-02, not a fork, not archived; Cargo.toml release profile lto = true, incremental = false. A second snippet now confirms the 249 MB/s / 82% unsafe-mode figure the record had as unconfirmed.
